technique: Spark SQL GROUP BY + window lag (YoY)
what_it_answers: How much electricity each state received per year and how fast it grows (only years with >= 330 reported days count as full years)

query: Q2 Top 10 peak days per state
what_it_answers: The ten days with the highest peak power supplied in each state, with the day's mean temperature

query: Q2 Season of each state's 30 highest peaks
what_it_answers: In which season does each state hit its highest peaks

query: Q2 Highest all-India days (sum of state peaks)
what_it_answers: Days with the highest SUM of state-level peaks. Note: state peaks happen at different hours, so this is not the same as the simultaneous national peak

query: Q3 Unmet peak demand by state and year
what_it_answers: How often and how severely each state's peak demand was not fully met

query: Q3 Unmet peak demand by grid region
what_it_answers: Regional shortfall pattern over the years

Observed association between daily mean temperature and demand. 'relative' divides each day by the state's average of that year to remove growth and state size. Association only - not proof of causation

query: Q4 Relative demand by temperature band
what_it_answers: Average relative demand in 5 degC temperature bands for each grid region

query: Q5 Monthly demand by state and year
what_it_answers: Month-by-month average daily demand for every state and year (heatmaps)
How much busier than an average day is each season in each region
How much lower (or higher) demand is on weekends than on weekdays in each state

query: Extra: All-India daily total with 30-day rolling mean
what_it_answers: All-India daily energy supplied (sum over states) and its 30-day rolling mean
